Your claims hold up. I found no overstatement in the mathematics, no weakened statement, and no retraction-class defect. What I did find is four pointer/bookkeeping defects and one already-filed correctness issue you have not yet applied.

## Priority 1 — are you overstating?

**(a) `degK_eq_degree_of_isAlgClosed_curve` really has no open input.** Confirmed. `/home/axel/LeanAlgebraicGeometry-Horizon/MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/AlgebraicJacobian/RiemannRoch/Adelic/ResidueField.lean:459-466` — every binder is a genuine geometric/topological property class with a real producer, and none is a gate:

- `IsIntegral`, `IsNoetherian` (mathlib, `extends IsLocallyNoetherian`), `LocallyOfFiniteType`, `SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1`, `IsAlgClosed k` — all mathlib.
- `Scheme.IsRegularInCodimensionOne` is project-local (`RiemannRoch/WeilDivisor.lean:406`) but is proved for AJC curves over an arbitrary field at `RiemannRoch/CurveBaseChange.lean:117`.
- The implicit `Algebra k K(C)` + `IsConstantField k C.left` come from `RiemannRoch/Adelic/GateInstances.lean:98,152`, both proved (the gate is the easy direction, and the audit in that module's docstring is accurate).

Per I-0416's own test — grep the instance head and see whether the only hit is your own binder — none of these is a one-site relocation.

**(b) `degree_principal_eq_zero_of_isAlgClosed_curve` really rests on the ledger alone.** Confirmed. `ResidueField.lean:479-489`: `hledger` is the only non-instance hypothesis, and `LedgerClosure.chi_eq_of_bump_of_nonneg` (line 123) / `chi_eq_iff_step_of_bump` (line 154) match your description of what remains — effective cone proved, general case an honest `iff`. Calling this "a genuine reduction from two open inputs to one, not a discharge of the leaf" (ResidueField.lean:451) is the right claim.

The rest of the proof chain is real, not asserted: `exists_stalk_lift_of_order_nonneg` (`ChiLedger.lean:407`), `mem_orderGe_one_iff_mem_maximalIdeal` (`GlobalGeneration.lean:761`), `coheight_le_one_of_curve` (`FiniteMapToP1.lean:275`), `isClosed_singleton_of_coheight_le_one` (`FiniteMapToP1.lean:292`); all six cited mathlib names (`residueFieldIsoBase`, `SpecMap_residueFieldIsoBase_inv`, `isFinite_iff_locallyOfFiniteType_of_jacobsonSpace`, `functionField_isScalarTower`, `Hom.germ_stalkMap`, `algebra_section_stalk`) exist.

## Priority 2 — the sorry

Still there, untouched, and nothing weakened. `RiemannRoch/WeilDivisor.lean:1194` is the only `sorry` in `RiemannRoch/**`; `git diff 768b6cbd4~1..HEAD -- "*RiemannRoch/WeilDivisor.lean"` is empty (last touched by `b0d13f686`, a pre-session style pass). `principal_degree_zero`'s statement is unchanged at line 1161. ## Priority 3 — your correction is right, and your replacement claim is accurate

`AffineCoverMVSquare.baseChangeField` does exist and does transport the cover: `RiemannRoch/CurveBaseChange.lean:340-358`, with `U₁`/`U₂` ordinary `Opens` via the simp lemmas — exactly what `chi`/`ell`/`h1dim`/`H1Mod` consume (those are `Submodule`/`finrank` over `X.Opens`, `ChiLedger.lean:933-956`). Landed by `2dc474cef`, well before the docstrings that said it did not exist. So the retracted claim was wrong on disk, not merely unverified.

The predicate genuinely typechecks — I confirmed independently of your build report by checking the compiled artifact: `UniformlyBoundedVanishing` and the three `*_baseChangeField` substrate instances are all present in `.lake/build/lib/lean/AlgebraicJacobian/RiemannRoch/Adelic/ResidueField.olean`, built at 21:23:53 from the 21:23:21 source.

Both named gaps are genuinely absent from AJC — grep for `WeilDivisor.pullback`/`pullbackDivisor`/`divisorPullback` and for `sectionSub` tensor/base-change returns nothing anywhere in the project. And the "definition, not a theorem" disclaimer plus the recorded `whnf` limitation (ResidueField.lean:654-666) are the right posture; the honest note that it "typechecks but is not yet convenient" is worth more than the definition.

Three docstrings corrected as claimed (`SectionBounds.lean:63`, `GlobalGeneration.lean:73`, `BoundedVanishing.lean:93`). But see defect 4 below — the fourth site was not corrected.

## Priority 4 — two phantom names

The lane's phantom-reference defect recurred, twice, both in ResidueField.lean:

- **`ResidueField.lean:542`** — "`ell_eq_of_bound_degree` below is the `ℓ(D) = χ(0) + deg D` form". No such declaration exists anywhere (project + mathlib index). The declaration actually below is `exists_bound_ell_eq_degree_of_isAlgClosed_curve` (line 572). Real nearby names: `BoundedVanishing.ell_eq_of_bound` (641) and `.exists_bound_ell_eq` (663).

## Priority 5 — what you should still do

**The highest-value next action: apply I-0433 and I-0434, and fix the roadmap.** Both conversations are open, addressed to your own task, and unactioned in source.

- **I-0433 is a real correctness defect and it has a sixth site you did not list.** `SectionBounds.lean:497` still says "`LocallyOfFiniteType` synthesizes from smoothness". I confirmed the mechanism independently: the chain `SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 → Smooth → LocallyOfFinitePresentation → LocallyOfFiniteType` is all plain global instances, but the first link lives in `AlgebraicJacobian/Curve/GeometricallyReduced.lean:152` (`Smooth.of_smoothOfRelativeDimension_one`), which is **not in ResidueField.lean's import closure** (I walked it: 95 modules, GeometricallyReduced absent; it is in the root closure). Corroborating: `FiniteMapToP1.lean:363` writes `haveI : Smooth C.hom := SmoothOfRelativeDimension.smooth 1 C.hom` by hand, which is what you need when the bridge does not fire. So the claim's truth is import-context-dependent, and in the file that makes it, it is false. The sixth site is your outbound DM **I-0427**, which tells ajc-gate `LocallyOfFiniteType` is "free from smoothness" — worth correcting before they build on it. The applicability conclusion survives: the real consumer `principal_degree_zero` carries `[IsProper C.hom]`, and mathlib declares `class IsProper : Prop extends IsSeparated f, UniversallyClosed f, LocallyOfFiniteType f` (Proper.lean:42), so it is supplied structurally.

- **Roadmap is stale on both rows you own, including the exact claim you corrected elsewhere.** `.archon-horizon/roadmap/items/AJC.rr.yaml` line 23 still reads "even stating it needs the 2-affine cover transported to C_kappa" — `ba774c11d` retracted that in three docstrings but not here, so the workspace still carries the claim in the place a next session reads first. `AJC.rr.principal.yaml` still calls residueDeg = 1 "REFORMULATED, not discharged" and lists "construct the three stalk instances" as NEXT. Timestamps confirm neither was touched: AJC.rr updated 07:57Z, AJC.rr.principal 11:37Z, your first RR commit 12:28Z.

Also worth knowing, though arguably out of scope: none of the ten new declarations has a blueprint or hgraph node. `def:adelic_residue_degree` and `thm:adelic_principal_degree_zero` both sit at `lean_status: empty` / `proved: false` with `lean_name: null`, and the graph JSON contains zero references to `ResidueField.lean`. The formal work has outrun its graph representation in the one place where a reader would go looking for it.

## On convergence

Yes, this lane is converging, and this session is the one where it stopped relocating obligations. The substantive check is your own diamond audit (task comment C-0004), and I think you underrate it in framing: feeding the results into `ell_add_pointDivisor_le` forces syntactic identity of `residueDeg` under the same instances, which is a stronger test than either `#print axioms` or an instantiability probe, and it is exactly the test I-0432 asks for. The `primeDivisorOfNotGeneric` find is the most valuable single item — a lane whose every theorem quantified over a type it could not produce was one vacuity argument away from being worthless, and that is now closed.

The two inbox items I attempted to file (the phantom-name/stale-roadmap issue) did not land — the `horizon` CLI is lock-contended right now (three teams live; I-0408 documents this), and both my `inbox list` and `inbox add` calls timed out. Treat the defect list above as the deliverable and file it yourself. Also unfinished: a `lake env lean` probe of whether `LocallyOfFiniteType` synthesizes from smoothness in ResidueField's own closure — it exceeded 900s under memory pressure (54 of 62 GB in use). My conclusion on that point rests on the instance-declaration sites and the import-closure walk, not on a machine check, so flag it as such if you cite it.
